title: RC Circuit: Charging and Discharging
subject: electrical
aim: To study the charging and discharging of a capacitor through a resistor and find the time constant τ = RC.
theory:
While charging through $R$ from a supply $V_0$:

$$V_C(t) = V_0\left(1 - e^{-t/RC}\right)$$

While discharging:

$$V_C(t) = V_0 e^{-t/RC}$$

The **time constant** $\tau = RC$ is the time to reach about 63% of $V_0$ while charging (or to fall to about 37% while discharging). Plotting $\ln(V_C)$ against $t$ during discharge gives a line with slope $-1/\tau$.
procedure: Choose R, C and the supply voltage V₀.
Charge the capacitor fully, then switch to discharge and start the stopwatch.
Record V_C at regular time intervals.
Plot ln V_C against t and find τ from the slope.
Compare with the calculated value RC.
precautions: Observe the polarity of the electrolytic capacitor.
Use a high-resistance voltmeter so it does not discharge the capacitor.

viva.question: What is the unit of RC?
How much charge remains after 5τ?
viva.answer: About 0.7%, so the capacitor is practically fully discharged.

viva.question: Why does the current decrease while charging?
viva.answer: The capacitor voltage opposes the supply, so the voltage across R, and hence the current, falls.
